newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEDNESDAY DIM MANCHESTER UNITED'S TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEDNESDAY DIM MANCHESTER UNITED'S TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Paul Scholes salvaged a point for Manchester United after Sheffield Wednesday's Benito Carbone had threatened to put the skids under the English premier league champions' title challenge at a rain-soaked Hillsborough on Wednesday.
Carbone fired Wednesday ahead with a 55th-minute curler but Scholes equalised six minutes later, lashing an unstoppable twenty-yard shot past Kevin Pressman.
The stalemate left United in sixth place, nine points adrift of leaders Liverpool ahead of the busy Christmas programme.

It was another disappointing result for United who have the worst away record of any of the top 10 teams in the premier league, with only two wins away from home -- a record they rarely looked like improving on against a lively Wednesday outfit unbeaten in seven games and inspired by Carbone's skilful promptings.

Second division Stockport County caused an upset in their League Cup fourth round replay with a 2-1 win at home over premier league West Ham to earn a place in the quarter-finals, the furthest they have ever reached in a major competition.
Stockport have also accounted for premier league Blackburn and first division Sheffield United in previous rounds.
All the goals came in the first half, Brett Angell scoring the winner as early as the 27th minute with a looping header over stranded goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko.
It had looked ominous for Stockport earlier when they fell behind to a Julian Dicks strike after 21 minutes but they levelled when Ian Dowie put through his own net less than 60 seconds later.
But Angell completed the scoring only five minutes later to earn Stockport a quarter-final meeting against premier league Southampton who won their fourth round replay against Oxford United 3-2.
